story.head: The Flames are going to let it fly
paras: The Flames (6-8-0) lost 5-2 to Colorado on Saturday, and the Sharks (7-7-1) lost 5-1 to Ottawa the same night. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Flames fifth (tied for 24th in the NHL) and the Sharks fourth (tied for 19th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.
The Flames’ record (.429) is about what their chances are worth. The Sharks’ record (.500) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.367), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Flames play some of the league’s fastest games (2nd), take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd) and have struggled on the power play (30th). On the other side, the Sharks do a lot of their shooting from distance (2nd lowest), are one of the league’s most physical teams (2nd) and ice the puck a lot (32nd). The Flames are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Sharks.

Joel Farabee (5 G / 10 A / 15 P in 14 GP) leads the Flames in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Matt Coronato (3 G / 11 A / 14 P in 14 GP) is next in line, with eight points in his last five games. The Sharks’ scoring runs through Macklin Celebrini (5 G / 11 A / 16 P in 13 GP), and Will Smith (6 G / 4 A / 10 P in 15 GP) has a team-high six goals.
Dustin Wolf (2-4-0 / .847 SV% in 6 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Calgary, but will likely start. Yaroslav Askarov (4-5-0 / .900 SV% in 9 GS) is in line to start for San Jose.
At home, Ryan Warsofsky likes to send Goodrow, Dellandrea and Ostapchuk out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Tsyplakov, Castagna and Klapka.
